definition_zh: 苗条的；微薄的；减肥
definition_en: thin in an attractive way, small in amount, or to try to become thinner
core_image: 一条合身的细腰长裙挂在衣架上
scene: 她每天游泳，一直保持着苗条的身材。 She stays slim by swimming every day.

senses.title: Attractively thin
senses.definition: thin in a healthy and attractive way

senses.example: She stays slim by swimming every day.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天游泳，一直保持着苗条的身材。
senses.why: This is the everyday body sense.

senses.title: Small in amount
senses.definition: small in amount or unlikely to happen

senses.title: Try to lose weight

senses.example: He is slimming for the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他为了夏天在减肥。
senses.why: The adjective became a verb of dieting.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为表示节食的动词。

definition_zh: 奖励；报酬；回报
definition_en: something given in return for good work or help

scene: 找回走失的小狗后，主人给了邻居一笔酬谢。 After the lost dog was found, the owner gave the neighbor a reward.

senses.title: Something given back
senses.definition: something given for good work or help

senses.example: A reward was offered for the missing ring.

senses.title: A good result

senses.why: What returns to you after effort is also a reward.

intro.en: Reward comes from Old French rewarder, to regard, related to regard.
intro.cn: reward 源自法语 rewarder（注视、看待），与 regard 同源。

items.en: Rewarder means to regard or consider.
items.cn: rewarder 意为注视或看待。

items.en: The prefix re- adds a sense of return.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 加上返回的含义。

items.en: Reward first means to regard with favour.
items.cn: reward 最初指以赞许的目光看待。

items.en: It becomes something given in return.
items.cn: 它变成回赠之物。

items.en: It also means the benefit of effort.
items.cn: 它也指努力带来的好处。

note.en: Reward returns something for effort; a prize is won in a contest.

senses.title: A small insect
senses.definition: a small insect or similar crawling creature

senses.example: A small bug crawled across the page.
senses.exampleCN: 一只小虫爬过书页。

senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，也是其他义项的来源。

senses.title: A fault in a machine or program
senses.definition: a small fault that stops something working properly
senses.definitionCN: 使某物无法正常运转的小毛病
senses.example: The program has a bug that hides the last line.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序有个故障，会隐藏最后一行。
senses.why: Early engineers found real insects stuck inside machines.
senses.whyCN: 早期工程师真的在机器里发现过卡住的虫子。

senses.example: They bugged the office for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在办公室装了一个月窃听器。

senses.whyCN: 藏起来的窃听器就像墙上的小虫在偷听。

senses.title: Make someone unsure
senses.definition: to make someone unable to understand or decide
senses.definitionCN: 使人无法理解或无法作出决定
senses.example: The instructions confused everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这些说明让屋里每个人都糊涂了。
senses.why: Too many choices at once leave the mind without a path.
senses.whyCN: 选择一次给得太多，脑子就找不到一条路。

senses.title: Mix two things up
senses.definition: to mistake one person or thing for another
senses.definitionCN: 把一个人或一样东西误认成另一个
senses.example: People often confuse the two words.
senses.exampleCN: 人们常常把这两个词混淆。
senses.why: Two things that look alike are stored in the mind almost on the same shelf.
senses.whyCN: 长得像的两样东西，在脑中几乎摆在同一层架子上。

intro.en: Confuse comes from Latin confundere, to pour together, from com-, together, and fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: confuse 来自拉丁语 confundere，意为倒在一起，由 com-（一起）与 fundere（倾倒）构成。

items.en: Fundere meant to pour a liquid out of a container.
items.cn: fundere 意为把液体从容器里倒出来。

items.en: Confundere meant to pour several things into one vessel.
items.cn: confundere 意为把几样东西倒进同一个容器。

items.en: The mixed result was hard to separate again.
items.cn: 混在一起之后，就很难再分开。

items.en: Old French confondre used the image for a confused mind.
items.cn: 古法语 confondre 把这个意象用于混乱的心思。

items.en: English confuse now means to puzzle someone or to mix two things up.
items.cn: 英语 confuse 如今指使人困惑，或把两样东西混淆。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like confuse, and the meaning group names other ways of puzzling someone.

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two paths in fog, then move to two similar forms and to two words on one shelf.

normal.en: Con- is together and fuse is pour, so confuse is to pour everything into one cup.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，fuse 是倒，所以 confuse 就是把所有东西倒进一个杯子。

normal.en: A confused mind is a drawer where every sock has the same colour.
normal.cn: 困惑的脑子，就像一个里面每只袜子都同色的抽屉。

normal.en: To confuse two words is to give them one name by mistake.
normal.cn: 混淆两个词，就是误把它们当成同一个名字。

normal.en: Confusing instructions make a simple task look like a maze.
normal.cn: 令人费解的说明，把简单任务变成迷宫。

normal.en: The fog does not move the road; it only hides which road is which.
normal.cn: 雾没有移动道路，只是藏起了哪条是哪条。

abstract.cn: 想象两种液体在同一只杯里相遇。

abstract.en: Picture two labels swapped on two jars.
abstract.cn: 想象两个罐子上的标签被互换。

examples.en: The map confused us more than it helped.
examples.cn: 这张地图没帮上忙，反而让我们更糊涂。

examples.en: Do not confuse being busy with being useful.

sensesIntro.en: From several liquids poured into one cup, to a mind that cannot tell two things apart.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two roads vanish into fog and two labels sit on the wrong jars.

branches.en: Being confused is a state of not knowing which way to go.

branches.en: Confusing two things means giving one the name of the other.

branches.en: Both senses come from a boundary that has stopped being visible.
branches.cn: 两个义项都来自一条已经看不见的界线。

branches.en: Clear steps are the best cure for a confused mind.
branches.cn: 清楚的步骤是治困惑最好的药。

branches.en: Look-alike words are the easiest pair to confuse.
branches.cn: 长得像的词，是最容易被混淆的一对。

intro.en: Confuse is built on Latin com-, together, plus fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: confuse 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 fundere（倾倒）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pour base fus- also appears in refuse, fusion and suffuse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的倾倒词基 fus- 也出现在 refuse、fusion 与 suffuse 中。

items.example: Do not confuse the two labels.
items.exampleCN: 不要把这两个标签弄混。
这个回答把我弄糊涂了。

items.example: The room was full of confusion.
She looked confused by the question.
items.exampleCN: 她似乎被这个问题问住了。

items.example: They refuse to change the date.

definition_zh: 凝视；盯着看；注视
definition_en: to look at something or someone for a long time with fixed eyes, without moving
core_image: 目光钉在一个点上——瞳孔不动，时间也不动
scene: 玻璃柜里的宝石在灯下闪着冷光。 The boy stared at the diamond ring without blinking.
sceneCN: 这里 stare 是「凝视」（第 1 个义项：长时间定睛注视）；句意为男孩目不转睛地盯着那枚钻戒。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加-ing 构成，义为「凝视（行为）」
拉丁借语，由 stare 加 decisis 构成，义为「遵循先例（法律原则）」

senses.title: To look long with fixed eyes
senses.definition: to look steadily for a long time, often without realizing it
senses.definitionCN: 长时间定睛注视，常是不自觉的
senses.example: He stared at the dark screen, thinking.
senses.exampleCN: 他盯着黑屏出神地想。
senses.why: The eyes are nailed to one point; nothing else moves.
senses.whyCN: 双眼被钉在一点上，其余一切静止。

senses.title: To look in a fixed way at nothing
senses.definition: to look straight ahead with an empty mind
senses.definitionCN: 目光直视前方而心不在焉
senses.example: She stared into space during the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会时她望着远方发呆。
senses.why: The eyes hold still even when the mind has left.
senses.whyCN: 心已走远，目光却仍停驻。

senses.title: To look openly and rudely
senses.definition: to look at someone too long and too openly, causing discomfort
senses.definitionCN: 过长、过直地看人，令人不适
senses.example: It's rude to stare at strangers on the train.
senses.exampleCN: 在火车上盯着陌生人看很失礼。
senses.why: A gaze fixed too long presses on the person looked at.
senses.whyCN: 停驻过久的目光对被看者形成压迫。

senses.title: To show a long fixed look
senses.definition: a long look with unmoving eyes
senses.definitionCN: 目光不动的长久注视
senses.example: She answered his stare with a smile.
senses.exampleCN: 她以微笑回应他的注视。
senses.why: The act becomes a thing you can meet or return.
senses.whyCN: 动作成为可迎、可回的东西。

senses.title: To face something obviously
senses.definition: in stare someone or something in the face, to be plainly present and unavoidable
senses.definitionCN: stare in the face 中指显而易见、无法回避
senses.example: Danger stared them in the face all night.
senses.exampleCN: 危险整夜直逼他们眼前。
senses.why: The fact holds its position until you look back at it.
senses.whyCN: 事实站在原地不动，直到你不得不回望。

intro.en: Stare comes from Germanic words for a fixed, rigid gaze, sharing old roots with the word stark.
intro.cn: stare 来自日耳曼语「目光僵直」之词，与 stark 共享古老的词根。

items.en: A root meaning "rigid, stiff" is generally reconstructed; the link is usually accepted.
items.cn: 一般认为词根表示「僵硬、挺直」；此关联通常被接受。

items.en: Germanic stark meant stiff, and star- words named the fixed gaze.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 stark 意为僵直，star- 词族指僵直的目光。

items.en: Old English starian meant to stare or to be stiff.
items.cn: 古英语 starian 意为凝视或僵硬。

items.en: The noun stare and the rude-look nuance developed.
items.cn: 名词 stare 与「失礼凝视」的细微义发展。

items.en: Latin stare decisis, "to stand by decisions", borrowed the word into law.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stare decisis「遵循既立决定」把该词借入法律。

note.en: Stare is homophones with the stair of buildings, and cousins with the gaze family.
note.cn: stare 与楼梯的 stair 同音，且与注视类词为亲。

entries.definition: one step of a staircase
entries.definitionCN: 楼梯一级；与 stare 同音但词源不同

entries.definition: to suffer from lack of food
stiff, plain, or severe; shares the rigid root
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬的；严酷的；与 stare 同根

entries.definition: to look steadily, often with feeling
to stare angrily
to look quickly and secretly
to stare with open mouth in surprise

normalIntro.en: Five real hooks for stare and its kin.
normalIntro.cn: 五条真实钩子帮助记住 stare。

normal.en: stare and stair sound alike: climb stairs, don't just stare.
normal.cn: stare 与 stair 同音：去爬梯，别光盯着。

normal.en: stare and stark share the stiff root: a stiff look.
normal.cn: stare 与 stark 同根：僵直的目光。

normal.en: a blank stare: the eyes open, the mind away.
normal.cn: a blank stare：眼睁着，心走了。

normal.en: glare = stare + anger; gaze = stare + feeling.
normal.cn: glare 是带怒的 stare；gaze 是带情的 stare。

normal.en: stare someone down: hold the look until they blink.
normal.cn: stare someone down：目光钉住对方直到其眨眼。

abstract.en: Feel your eyes lock onto one point and forget the room.
abstract.cn: 感受目光锁住一点，忘了整个房间。

abstract.en: See a cat fixed on a mouse hole, unmoving.
abstract.cn: 看见猫一动不动盯住鼠洞。

abstract.en: Hear silence grow as two gazes hold each other.
abstract.cn: 听沉默在两道对视中生长。

examples.en: She stared at the letter, unable to speak.
examples.cn: 她盯着那封信，说不出话。

examples.en: Don't stare; it makes people uncomfortable.
examples.cn: 别盯着人看，那让人不舒服。

examples.en: The mountain stared down at the tiny village.
examples.cn: 高山俯瞰着小小的村庄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯黛尔」——像「死盯」：双眼死死钉住一点，一动不动。

root: 古英语 starian「凝视」，属日耳曼语源，与 stark「僵直」共享表示「僵硬、挺直」的词根（重构形式，通常被接受）；确切印欧形式来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Stare keeps one image: eyes nailed to a point while the world waits.
sensesIntro.cn: stare 只有一个意象：目光钉在一点上，世界静候。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes fixed stiffly on one point
core.cn: 核心意象：目光僵直地钉在一点上

branches.en: long looks at things and into nothing
branches.cn: 对物之凝视与对空之出神

branches.en: a look held too long on people
branches.cn: 在人身上停留过久的目光

branches.en: the look as a thing returned
branches.cn: 作为可回应之物的注视

branches.en: facts that hold their ground until seen
branches.cn: 站定不动逼人正视的事实

branches.en: the plain gaze sense
branches.cn: 单纯的注视义项

intro.en: Stare is a bare verb; its family grows by compounds with the eyes and the mind.
intro.cn: stare 是光杆动词；其词族围绕眼睛与心灵复合生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare "to stand" borrowed the shape for law Latin, but the English word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stare「站立」被借入法律拉丁语；英语本词则属日耳曼语源。

items.example: Staring at screens all day tires the eyes.
items.exampleCN: 整天盯屏幕让眼睛疲劳。

items.example: He gave a blank stare at the question.
items.exampleCN: 他对问题报以茫然一瞥。

items.example: The stark truth was hard to hear.

items.meaning: to win a contest of looks
items.exampleCN: 她以目光压倒了起哄者。

items.example: He stared into space for a while.
items.exampleCN: 他望着虚空发了会儿呆。

items.example: They gazed at the harbor lights.
items.exampleCN: 他们凝望着港口的灯火。

items.example: The teacher's glare silenced the room.
items.exampleCN: 老师的怒视让全屋安静。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加-ing 构成，义为「凝视」

definition_zh: 哲学；思想体系；人生准则；哲理；达观
definition_en: the study of the most basic questions about existence, knowledge, values, and reason; a system of ideas held by a person or group
core_image: 一个人放下手里的急事，转身追问「这一切究竟凭什么」
scene: 她的人生哲学很简单：努力工作，保持好奇。 Her philosophy is simple: work hard and stay curious.
sceneCN: 这里 philosophy 是「一个人奉行的人生准则」（第 3 个义项：准则）；句意：她的人生准则很简单：努力工作，保持好奇。场景要点：不是学科、是一套自持的态度；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 哲学；思想体系；人生准则；达观

derivatives.zh: 哲学家；达观的人
哲学的；达观的
作哲学思考；空谈哲理
从哲学上；达观地

senses.title: The academic study of first questions
senses.titleCN: 哲学学科：追问最根本的问题
senses.definition: the academic study of the most basic questions about existence, knowledge, truth, values, and reason
senses.definitionCN: 对存在、知识、真理、价值与理性等最根本问题的学术研究
senses.example: She took up philosophy after a first course in logic.
senses.exampleCN: 上完一门逻辑学入门课之后，她开始研读哲学。
senses.why: The Greek word names a love of wisdom. A discipline that pursues wisdom for its own sake became a faculty, then a degree subject.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词本意是“爱智慧”。一门为智慧本身而追求智慧的学问，后来成了一个学科门类、一个学位专业。

senses.title: A system of thought
senses.titleCN: 思想体系：一套自成一体的说法
senses.definition: a particular system of ideas about the world, often named after its founder
senses.definitionCN: 关于世界的一套特定观念体系，常以其创立者命名
senses.example: His early work was shaped by German idealist philosophy.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期的工作受到德国唯心主义哲学体系的影响。
senses.why: A discipline that keeps asking first questions produces rival answers. Each coherent set of answers becomes a philosophy with a name.
senses.whyCN: 一门不停追问根本问题的学科会产出彼此竞争的答案。每一套自洽的答案就变成了一个有名字的哲学体系。

senses.title: Guiding principles for living
senses.titleCN: 人生准则：拿来过日子的一套道理
senses.definition: the set of principles that guides a person's or an organization's behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指导个人或组织行为的一套原则
senses.example: Our philosophy is to fix the cause, not just the symptom.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的准则是解决病根，而不只是处理症状。
senses.why: The grand system shrinks to the scale of one life. What a person treats as first principles becomes their working philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的体系缩到一个人的尺度。一个人当作根本原则的东西，就成了他行事的准则。

senses.title: Calm acceptance of difficulty
senses.titleCN: 达观：把坏事放回它该有的尺寸
senses.definition: a calm attitude toward trouble, based on seeing it as part of a larger picture
senses.definitionCN: 面对困顿时的一种平静态度，源于把它看成更大图景的一部分
senses.example: He accepted the loss with philosophy and went back to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他达观地接受了损失，又回去工作了。
senses.why: The discipline trains you to see events against a wider frame. That habit, applied to daily misfortune, shows up as composure.
senses.whyCN: 这门学问训练你把事件放进更宽的框架里看。这个习惯用到日常的不幸上，表现出来就是沉着。

senses.title: The philosophy of a special field
senses.titleCN: 某领域的哲学：先问这门学问凭什么
senses.definition: the critical study of the assumptions and methods of a particular subject, such as science, law, or history
senses.definitionCN: 对某一学科（如科学、法律、历史）的前提与方法所作的批判性研究
senses.example: Philosophy of law asks what makes a rule legally valid.
senses.exampleCN: 法哲学追问：是什么使一条规则具有法律效力。
senses.why: Every field rests on assumptions it cannot prove from inside. Philosophy is called in to examine those foundations.
senses.whyCN: 每个领域都建立在它内部无法证明的前提上。哲学被请来检查这些地基。

senses.title: The principles behind a practice
senses.titleCN: 理念：一套做法背后的道理
senses.definition: the set of ideas and aims that explain why something is done the way it is
senses.definitionCN: 解释某件事为何这样做的一套观念与目标
senses.example: The school's philosophy of teaching puts questions before answers.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校的教学理念把问题放在答案之前。
senses.why: Any practice can be asked for its rationale. The rationale, stated as principles, is its philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 任何做法都可以被追问理由。把这些理由表述为原则，就是它的理念。

senses.title: The ancient love of wisdom
senses.titleCN: 爱智：最早的那种生活方式
senses.definition: the original Greek pursuit of wisdom through reasoned inquiry, before it became an academic subject
senses.definitionCN: 希腊人最早通过理性探究追求智慧的生活方式，尚在它成为学科之前
senses.example: In Plato's dialogues, philosophy is a way of life rather than a job.
senses.exampleCN: 在柏拉图的对话里，哲学是一种生活方式而不是一份职业。
senses.why: Philosophia literally means love of wisdom. The historical sense keeps the desire rather than the syllabus.
senses.whyCN: philosophia 字面就是“爱智慧”。这个历史义保留的是那份渴望，而不是课程表。

senses.title: The habit of questioning assumptions
senses.titleCN: 追问前提：不接受「向来如此」
senses.definition: a critical habit of asking what an accepted belief rests on
senses.definitionCN: 一种批判性的习惯：追问一个被接受的看法究竟依托于什么
senses.example: Bring some philosophy to the meeting and ask why this rule exists.
senses.exampleCN: 带点哲学思辨进会场，问问这条规定为什么存在。
senses.why: Strip away the subject matter and what remains is a move: refuse to let a premise pass unexamined.
senses.whyCN: 剥掉具体内容，剩下的就是一个动作：不让任何一个前提未经检查就过关。

intro.en: Philosophy is a Greek compound meaning love of wisdom. The word names an attitude before it names a subject, and English borrowed it through Latin and French.
intro.cn: philosophy 是一个意为“爱智慧”的希腊复合词。它先命名的是一种态度，后来才命名一门学科；英语是经拉丁语和法语接手的。

items.en: Philos meant 'dear, beloved, loving'. It described affection and close friendship rather than abstract approval.
items.cn: philos 意为“亲爱的、被爱的、爱着的”。它描述的是亲近与友情，而不是抽象的赞同。

items.en: Sophia meant 'wisdom, skill, cleverness'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; some sources connect it with sophos 'wise' and possibly with words for clarity. This part of the chain is not firmly established.
items.cn: sophia 意为“智慧、技艺、聪明”。它更早的来源不确定；有说法把它与 sophos“智慧的”以及表示“清楚”的词联系起来。这一段词源链并无定论。

items.en: Philos plus sophia gave philosophia, 'the love of wisdom'. The word is associated with Pythagoras by later ancient reports, though the attribution is traditional rather than documented.
items.cn: philos 加 sophia 构成 philosophia“爱智慧”。后世古籍把这个词与毕达哥拉斯联系起来，但这属于传统说法，缺乏直接文献证据。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word unchanged in sense. Cicero and others used it for the Greek tradition of reasoned inquiry.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入这个希腊词，含义不变。西塞罗等人用它来指希腊那条理性探究的传统。

items.en: Old French shortened and reshaped the word as filosofie, which is the form English received around 1300.
items.cn: 古法语把词形缩短、改造为 filosofie，英语约在 1300 年接受的就是这个形式。

items.en: From the 19th century the word also names a university department and its curriculum. The older sense of a way of life survives in phrases like with philosophy.
items.cn: 19 世纪起，这个词也指大学的院系及其课程。较古老的“生活方式”义则保存在 with philosophy 这类短语里。

note.en: The first group shares the philo- or soph- pieces but not always the whole meaning. The second group collects words for systems of belief.
note.cn: 第一组共享 philo- 或 soph- 构件，但未必整体同义。第二组收表示信仰体系的词。

entries.definition: a person who studies or practises philosophy. Philosophy plus -er, the person who loves wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或实践哲学的人。philosophy 加 -er，即爱智慧的人。

entries.definition: relating to philosophy, or calm in the face of trouble. The adjective covers both the academic and the composed senses.
entries.definitionCN: 与哲学有关的，或面对困顿时平静的。这个形容词同时覆盖学科义与达观义。

entries.definition: the study of language and texts historically. Philo- 'loving' plus logos 'word', so 'love of words', not love of wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 对语言与文本的历史研究。philo-“爱”加 logos“言词”，是“爱言词”，不是爱智慧。

entries.definition: clever but misleading argument. From sophos 'wise', but the word marks cleverness used to deceive rather than wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 巧妙却误导人的论证。源自 sophos“智慧的”，但这个词标记的是用于欺骗的机巧，而非智慧。

entries.definition: the activity or product of thinking. Thought is broader and looser; philosophy is organized and argues from principles.
entries.definitionCN: 思考活动或其产物。thought 更宽更松；philosophy 是有组织、从原则出发论证的。

entries.definition: a system of beliefs held by a group, often political. Ideology stresses shared social belief; philosophy stresses reasoned inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 群体持有的一套信念，常指政治的。ideology 强调群体共享的信念；philosophy 强调理性探究。

entries.definition: a set of beliefs taught by a religion or school. Doctrine is received and taught; philosophy invites challenge.
entries.definitionCN: 宗教或学派所传授的一套信念。doctrine 是被接受、被讲授的；philosophy 则欢迎质疑。

entries.definition: the overall way a person sees the world. Worldview can be unspoken and unexamined; philosophy is the examined version.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人看世界的总体方式。worldview 可以是未言明、未检查的；philosophy 是经过检查的版本。

entries.definition: the basic rules a person follows. Principles are the content; philosophy is the reasoned framework that holds them together.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人遵循的基本规则。principles 是内容；philosophy 是把它们统摄起来的理性框架。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the two Greek halves, the Pythagoras story, the difference from philology, the calm acceptance, and the meeting-room question.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：两个希腊半边、毕达哥拉斯的传说、与 philology 的区别、达观、以及会议室里的那一问。

normal.en: Philo- = loving, -sophy = wisdom. Philosophy is love of wisdom, spelled out in two halves.
normal.cn: philo-＝爱，-sophy＝智慧。philosophy 就是“爱智慧”，两个半边拼得明明白白。

normal.en: Pythagoras is said to have coined it: he called himself a lover of wisdom, not a possessor of it.
normal.cn: 据说毕达哥拉斯造了这个词：他称自己是智慧的热爱者，而不是占有者。

normal.en: Philology loves words, philosophy loves wisdom. Same prefix, different object.
normal.cn: philology 爱言词，philosophy 爱智慧。前缀相同，对象不同。

normal.en: With philosophy means carrying trouble lightly, as if it were one small item in a very large frame.
normal.cn: with philosophy 是把困顿拿得很轻，仿佛它只是一个极大画框里的小物件。

normal.en: In a meeting, philosophy is the person who asks why this rule exists at all.
normal.cn: 在会上，philosophy 就是那个问“这条规定到底为什么存在”的人。

abstract.en: Philosophy is what remains when you refuse to let any premise pass without asking what holds it up.
abstract.cn: 哲学就是当你拒绝让任何前提未经追问就过关时，剩下的那种活动。

abstract.en: A philosophy is a map of the whole drawn by someone who has never seen the whole.
abstract.cn: 一套哲学是一个从未见过整体的人画出的整体地图。

abstract.en: Wisdom is not a possession one can hold; the word's geometry is a reaching toward, not an arrival.
abstract.cn: 智慧不是可以握有的东西；这个词的几何形状是“伸向”，而不是“抵达”。

examples.en: He studied philosophy for four years before turning to artificial intelligence.
examples.cn: 他学了四年哲学，之后转向人工智能。

examples.en: Their company philosophy is that a slow correct decision beats a fast wrong one.
examples.cn: 他们的公司理念是：慢慢做对的决定胜过匆匆做错的决定。

examples.en: She took the criticism with philosophy and revised the paper that same week.
examples.cn: 她达观地接受了批评，并在同一周修改了论文。

dict_mnemonic.text: “费罗索菲”——费罗（philo，爱）追着索菲（sophia，智慧）跑，一路追问到底，就是哲学

intro.en: The family is built from two Greek nouns joined by a combining vowel, then extended with ordinary English endings for people, adjectives, and verbs.

senses.title: A sudden dangerous situation
senses.definition: a sudden serious event that requires immediate attention
senses.definitionCN: 突然发生、需要立即处理的严重事件
senses.example: The emergency exit was blocked by boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 紧急出口被箱子堵住了。
senses.why: The noun began as an unforeseen occurrence that suddenly rises up, so emergency is a situation that breaks through ordinary routine without warning.

senses.title: Used for such a situation

senses.definitionCN: 为突发危险局面设计或保存的
senses.example: They kept an emergency fund for hard times.
senses.exampleCN: 他们存了一笔应急资金以备难关。
senses.why: A thing reserved for the sudden event borrows the event's name, so an exit, fund or room can all be called emergency.

senses.title: An unforeseen occurrence, in older use

definition_en: to go somewhere with someone, to happen or exist together with something, or to play music in support of a performer
core_image: 两个人并排走，一个人的步子跟着另一个人的步子
scene: 演出前的后台很安静，歌手在钢琴边等灯光亮起。 A young pianist accompanied her on the old upright piano.
sceneCN: 这里 accompany 指「为演唱者伴奏」（第 6 个义项：用乐器为表演者伴奏）；句意为一位年轻钢琴手用那架旧立式钢琴为她伴奏。

pos.zh: 动词：陪伴；陪同；伴随；附有；伴奏

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「伴奏；伴随物」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「伴奏者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「附随的；同时发生的」
由否定前缀 un- 加过去分词构成，义为「无人陪同的；无伴奏的」

senses.title: To go somewhere with someone
senses.definition: to travel or go somewhere together with another person, as a companion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为同伴与另一个人一起走或去某处
senses.example: Her brother accompanied her to the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 她哥哥陪她去了机场。
senses.why: The Latin word began as 'one who shares bread'; sharing the road grows straight out of sharing a meal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词原本指「一起分面包的人」；一起分过面包，就很自然地走到一起上路。

senses.title: To escort someone politely
senses.definition: to go with someone to a place or to the door, especially in order to be polite or to protect them
senses.definitionCN: 指陪某人走到某处或门口，尤指出于礼貌或保护
senses.example: The host accompanied us to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 主人把我们送到大门口。
senses.why: A companion who walks a guest out turns the shared road into a small act of courtesy.
senses.whyCN: 陪客人走出去的同伴，把「共走一段路」变成了一种小小的礼节。

senses.title: To happen at the same time as
senses.definition: of an event, condition, or symptom, to occur together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 指事件、状况或症状与另一事物同时出现
senses.example: The fever is often accompanied by a sore throat.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧常常伴有喉咙痛。
senses.why: Walking together becomes happening together: two things keep the same pace without either one causing the other.
senses.whyCN: 「一起走」变成「一起发生」：两件事步调一致，但谁也不必然引起谁。

senses.title: To be supplied together with
senses.definition: of a document, object, or item, to be provided together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 指文件、物品或附件与另一事物一起提供
senses.example: The application must be accompanied by two photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 申请材料必须附上两张照片。
senses.why: The thing that travels with the main thing is a companion in the literal sense: it never arrives alone.
senses.whyCN: 与主体一起走的东西就是字面意义上的同伴：它从不单独到达。

senses.title: To be served with a food or drink
senses.definition: of a drink or dish, to be served together with a particular food because the two go well together
senses.definitionCN: 指某种饮料或菜肴与特定食物搭配供应，因为二者相配
senses.example: A light white wine accompanies the fish course.
senses.exampleCN: 这道鱼配一款清淡的白葡萄酒。
senses.why: At the table the companion is the dish or drink that keeps the main course company.
senses.whyCN: 在餐桌上，同伴就是陪着主菜的那道菜或那杯酒。

senses.title: To play music in support of a performer
senses.definition: to play an instrument while someone sings or plays the main part
senses.definitionCN: 指在别人演唱或演奏主旋律时用乐器伴奏
senses.example: A young pianist accompanied her on the old upright piano.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年轻钢琴手用那架旧立式钢琴为她伴奏。
senses.why: In music the supporter literally walks beside the soloist, note for note, without taking the lead.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里，支持者确实与独奏者并肩而行，一个音一个音地跟着，却不抢主位。

senses.title: To accompany oneself
senses.definition: in the phrase accompany oneself, to sing while playing an instrument for one's own support
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 accompany oneself，指一边演唱一边用乐器为自己伴奏
senses.example: He accompanied himself on the guitar at the small bar.
senses.exampleCN: 他在小酒吧里抱着吉他自弹自唱。
senses.why: The companion and the soloist collapse into one person, but the two roles stay separate in the grammar.
senses.whyCN: 同伴与独唱者合成了一个人，但这两个角色在语法上仍然分开。

senses.title: To add a gesture alongside words
senses.definition: to do something at the same time as speaking or acting, so that the two support each other
senses.definitionCN: 指在说话或行动的同时做另一件事，使二者互相配合
senses.example: He accompanied the warning with a shake of his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他一边警告，一边摇了摇头。
senses.why: Any action that walks beside another action is a companion; a gesture can accompany a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 任何与另一动作并肩而行的动作都是同伴；一个手势可以陪伴一句话。

intro.en: Accompany goes back to a Latin phrase for sharing bread, and the word still means keeping someone company.
intro.cn: accompany 可追溯到拉丁语中「分面包」的说法，这个词至今仍表示与人为伴。

items.en: Panis meant 'bread'; it is generally connected with pascere 'to feed, graze', though the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: panis 意为「面包」；一般认为与 pascere「喂养、放牧」有关，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Com- 'with' plus panis formed companio, 'one who shares bread with another'.
items.cn: com-「与」加 panis 构成 companio，意为「与他人分面包的人」。

items.en: Old French compaign meant 'companion', and the verb acompaignier meant 'to join someone as a companion'.
items.cn: 古法语 compaign 意为「同伴」，动词 acompaignier 意为「作为同伴加入某人」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; the musical sense is recorded from the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词；音乐义从十八世纪起有记录。

items.en: The passive form be accompanied by became a fixed pattern for symptoms, documents, and sounds.
items.cn: 被动形式 be accompanied by 成为描述症状、文件与声音的固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same bread root; the near-meaning group lists other ways of going along with someone.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「面包」词根的一族词；近义组列出其他「与人同行」的说法。

entries.definition: The music or thing that goes with a main part.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴奏、伴随物」，指与主体相配的音乐或事物。

entries.definition: A musician who plays for a singer or a soloist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴奏者」，指为歌手或独奏者伴奏的音乐家。

entries.definition: Without anyone or anything going along; also used of music with no accompaniment.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无人陪同的、无伴奏的」，指没有同伴或没有伴奏。

entries.definition: A person who spends time with you, sharing the same bread root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同伴、伙伴」，与本词共享「面包」词根。

entries.definition: The state of being with others, or a business, also from the bread root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陪伴、公司」，同样出自「面包」词根。

entries.definition: To go with someone to protect or guide them, more formal than accompany.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「护送、陪同」，比 accompany 更正式，带有保护或引导意味。

entries.definition: To go with someone as a servant or official helper, an old formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「随行、侍候」，是很旧的正式用法，指作为随从或助手同行。

entries.definition: To travel with vehicles or ships in order to protect them.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「护送、护航」，指为车辆或船只护行。

entries.definition: To go with young people to keep them safe and well behaved.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「陪同监护」，指陪着年轻人以保证安全与规矩。

entries.definition: To play music behind a singer, an informal word for the musical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「为……伴奏、在背后支持」，是音乐义的口语说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real bread root and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的「面包」词根，以及这个词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: panis is bread: a companion is someone you share bread with.
normal.cn: panis 是「面包」：companion 就是和你分面包的人。

normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 companion、company 与 companionship。

normal.en: To accompany someone is to keep them company on the road.
normal.cn: to accompany someone 就是在路上与某人作伴。

normal.en: Be accompanied by is the pattern for symptoms and documents.

normal.en: An accompanist is the player who walks beside the soloist.

abstract.en: Two pairs of footprints in the same snow, one set always half a step behind.
abstract.cn: 同一片雪地上有两行脚印，其中一行总落后半步。

abstract.en: A companion can be a person, a fever, a photograph or a chord; what matters is that it never arrives alone.
abstract.cn: 同伴可以是一个人、一场发烧、一张照片或一个和弦；关键在于它从不单独到来。

abstract.en: To accompany is to lend your step to someone else's direction.
abstract.cn: 陪伴就是把自己的脚步借给别人的方向。

sensesIntro.en: Accompany begins with two people sharing bread and walking the same road, then spreads to symptoms, documents, dishes, music, and even a gesture that follows a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: accompany 从两个人分面包、同走一条路开始，随后扩展到症状、文件、菜肴、音乐，甚至扩展到跟着一句话出现的手势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people walk side by side, one step keeping time with the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人并排走，一个人的步子跟着另一个人的步子。

branches.en: THE PERSON: walking beside a friend, or politely seeing a guest out.
branches.cn: 人物线：走在朋友身旁，或礼貌地把客人送出门。

branches.en: THE EVENT: two things keep pace, such as a fever and a sore throat.
branches.cn: 事件线：两件事步调一致，例如发烧与喉咙痛。

branches.en: THE THING: the photograph with an application and the wine with a fish course.
branches.cn: 物品线：随申请附上的照片，以及配鱼的葡萄酒。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: a pianist beside a singer, or a singer playing for himself.
branches.cn: 音乐线：歌手身旁的钢琴手，或自己为自己弹唱的歌手。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: a shake of the head that goes along with a warning.
branches.cn: 动作线：跟着一句警告一起出现的摇头。

intro.en: Accompany entered English as a French verb, and English added familiar endings to build the family.

definition_zh: 揭示；透露；显露
definition_en: to make something known or visible that was hidden
core_image: 一块幕布被拉开，后面的景象突然出现在眼前
scene: 调查揭示了一个令人震惊的事实。 The investigation revealed a shocking fact.
sceneCN: 这里 reveal 是「揭示」（第 1 个义项：让原本隐藏的事情为人所知）；句意：调查揭示了一个令人震惊的事实。

senses.title: Make known
senses.definition: to make a fact or secret known
senses.definitionCN: 使事实或秘密为人所知
senses.example: The report revealed serious problems.
senses.exampleCN: 报告揭示了严重问题。
senses.why: The Latin source means to draw back a veil, so revealing uncovers what was hidden.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为拉开面纱，因此 reveal 就是揭开被遮住的东西。

senses.title: Make visible
senses.definition: to show something that was not visible before
senses.definitionCN: 使之前看不见的东西显示出来
senses.example: The curtain rose and revealed a bright stage.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布升起，露出明亮的舞台。
senses.why: Pulling away a cover makes the hidden scene visible.
senses.whyCN: 拉开遮盖物，就使隐藏的景象可见。

senses.title: A divine disclosure
senses.definition: to make a religious truth known
senses.definitionCN: 使宗教真理为人所知
senses.example: The prophet revealed a message to the people.
senses.exampleCN: 先知向人们启示了一条信息。
senses.why: Religious language uses the veil image for truths made known by God.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言用揭幕的意象，表示由神显明的真理。

intro.en: Reveal comes from Latin revelare, to draw back a veil, from velum, a veil.
intro.cn: reveal 源自拉丁语 revelare（拉开面纱），来自 velum（面纱）。

items.en: Velum means a veil or curtain.
items.cn: velum 意为面纱或帘子。

items.en: Revelare means to draw back a veil.
items.cn: revelare 意为拉开面纱。

items.en: Reveler means to disclose.
items.cn: reveler 意为揭露。

items.en: Reveal covers facts and hidden scenes.
items.cn: reveal 涵盖事实与隐藏景象。

items.en: Revelation also names sudden understanding.
items.cn: revelation 也指突然的领悟。

note.en: Reveal is close to disclose and uncover, with the image of a lifted veil.
note.cn: reveal 与披露、揭开相近，带有拉起面纱的意象。

entries.definition: a surprising disclosure
showing hidden truth
someone who reveals

normalIntro.en: Reveal is pulling back a veil: the hidden face appears.
normalIntro.cn: reveal 就是拉开面纱：隐藏的面孔显露出来。

normal.en: Reveal the truth means show what really happened.
normal.cn: reveal the truth 意为说明真实发生的事。

normal.en: Reveal a secret means tell what was hidden.
normal.cn: reveal a secret 意为说出隐藏的秘密。

normal.en: Reveal itself means become visible by itself.
normal.cn: reveal itself 意为自行显现。

normal.en: A revealing detail shows more than expected.
normal.cn: a revealing detail 显露出超出预期的信息。

normal.en: Compare disclose: disclose is formal and factual, reveal often has a dramatic image.
normal.cn: 对比 disclose：disclose 正式而平实，reveal 常带戏剧性意象。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain pulled aside on a lit stage.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布在灯光明亮的舞台前被拉开。

abstract.en: Imagine a fog lifting from a mountain.
abstract.cn: 想象雾气从山上散开。

abstract.en: Think of a letter opened after many years.
abstract.cn: 想象多年后拆开的一封信。

examples.en: The letter revealed a family secret.
examples.cn: 这封信揭示了一个家庭秘密。

examples.en: The clouds parted and revealed the moon.
examples.cn: 云层散开，露出了月亮。

examples.en: Tests revealed a small problem in the engine.
examples.cn: 检测显示发动机有一个小问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（去掉）＋ veal（面纱）」——把面纱拿掉，真相就露出来；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: Reveal first makes a fact known, then makes something visible, and in religious use means a truth disclosed by God.
sensesIntro.cn: reveal 先指让事实为人所知，再指使事物可见，在宗教用法中指神所显明的真理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain drawn back to show a hidden scene.
core.cn: 核心意象：幕布被拉开，露出隐藏景象。

branches.en: Making facts known is the main sense.
branches.cn: 让事实为人所知是主要义项。

branches.en: Making something visible is the physical image.
branches.cn: 使事物可见是具体的意象。

branches.en: Religious truth is revealed from above.
branches.cn: 宗教真理是从上而来的启示。

branches.en: Pulling back the cover shows both scene and truth.
branches.cn: 拉开遮盖既露出景象，也露出真相。

branches.en: A revelation can be ordinary or sacred.
branches.cn: 启示可以是普通的，也可以是神圣的。

latinIntro.cn: revelare 意为拉开面纱。

definition_zh: 承认；认错；确认收到；致谢；认可
definition_en: to admit that something is true, to confirm that you have received something, or to show recognition and thanks
core_image: 收到信后回一句「我看到了」，让对面那个人放下悬着的心
scene: 他发出邮件后一直盯着手机，只等一句回话。 Please acknowledge my email so I know you received it.
sceneCN: 这里 acknowledge 指「告知已收到」（第 3 个义项：确认收到某物）；句意为请回复确认你已收到我的邮件，好让我知道。

pos.zh: 动词：承认；认错；确认收到；致谢；认可

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「承认；致谢；收到通知」
同上的英式拼写，义为「承认；致谢；确认收到」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「公认的；得到承认的」
由 un- 加本词加 -ed 构成，义为「未被承认的；未获答复的」

senses.title: Admit that something is true
senses.definition: to accept or admit that a fact, situation or claim is true
senses.definitionCN: 接受或承认某个事实、情况或说法是真实的
senses.example: She acknowledged that the delay was her fault.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认延误是她的责任。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to know and then to recognize; acknowledging is saying out loud what you already know to be true.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「知道」，进一步引申为「认出」；承认就是把心里已经知道为真的东西说出来。

senses.title: Admit a fault or responsibility
senses.definition: to admit that you did something wrong or that you are responsible for it
senses.definitionCN: 承认自己做错了事，或承认自己对此负有责任
senses.example: The company finally acknowledged its role in the pollution.
senses.exampleCN: 公司最终承认了自己在污染中所起的作用。
senses.why: Knowing a fault and naming it are two different steps; the word marks the second, harder step.
senses.whyCN: 知道自己有错，与把错说出口，是两步；这个词标出的是更难的那一步。

senses.title: Confirm that something has arrived
senses.definition: to tell someone that you have received a message, letter, order or payment
senses.definitionCN: 告诉对方已收到某封信、某条消息、某笔订单或款项
senses.example: Please acknowledge my email so I know you received it.
senses.exampleCN: 请回复确认你已收到我的邮件，好让我知道。
senses.why: A message only counts as delivered when the other side shows that it has registered it, so recognition becomes receipt.
senses.whyCN: 一条消息只有在对方表示「已登记」时才算真正送达，于是「认出」变成了「确认收到」。

senses.title: Thank someone for help
senses.definition: to publicly thank a person or group for their help or support
senses.definitionCN: 公开感谢某人或某个群体给予的帮助与支持
senses.example: The author acknowledged her students in the preface.
senses.exampleCN: 作者在序言里向学生们致谢。
senses.why: To recognize a kindness is also to admit a debt, so thanks and admission share one verb.
senses.whyCN: 承认别人的好意，也就等于承认自己欠了一份情；于是致谢与承认共用一个动词。

senses.title: Recognize a right or authority
senses.definition: to accept the existence or validity of someone's right, status or power
senses.definitionCN: 接受某人的权利、地位或权力确实存在并有效
senses.example: The government acknowledged the union's right to strike.
senses.exampleCN: 政府承认了工会罢工的权利。
senses.why: Recognition is the first act of acceptance: once you acknowledge a right, you can no longer pretend it is not there.
senses.whyCN: 认可是接受的第一步：一旦承认某项权利存在，就再也不能假装它不存在。

senses.title: Greet with a small nod
senses.definition: to greet someone with a small movement of the head or a brief smile
senses.definitionCN: 用轻微点头或短暂微笑与人打招呼
senses.example: He acknowledged me with a nod and kept walking.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝我点了点头，继续往前走。
senses.why: A nod is the smallest possible act of recognition, and the word names that physical sign.
senses.whyCN: 点头是最小的一次「认出」，这个词就把这个身体动作收进自己的意思里。

senses.title: Show that you have noticed someone
senses.definition: to show by word or gesture that you have seen a person who is present
senses.definitionCN: 用言语或动作表示你看见了在场的某个人
senses.example: She walked past me without acknowledging me.
senses.exampleCN: 她从我身边走过，完全没有理睬我。
senses.why: Not acknowledging someone is a deliberate act of not-knowing; the word measures how much recognition a person is given.
senses.whyCN: 不理睬，是故意「装着不认识」；这个词因此也用来衡量一个人得到了多少承认。

senses.title: Be publicly recognized as
senses.definition: to be generally recognized or accepted as having a certain quality or position
senses.definitionCN: 被普遍认可或接受具有某种品质或地位
senses.example: She is widely acknowledged as the finest cellist of her generation.
senses.exampleCN: 她被公认为同代人中最出色的大提琴手。
senses.why: When many people recognize the same thing, private knowledge becomes public standing, and the passive form carries that shared verdict.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人都认出同一件事，私下的了解就成了公开的定评，被动形式承载的正是这份公认。

intro.en: Acknowledge is not a Latin word: it grew out of the Old English verb for knowing, with its ending later rebuilt on the model of knowledge.
intro.cn: acknowledge 不是拉丁词：它从古英语表示「知道」的动词长出来，词尾后来照着 knowledge 的样子重塑。

items.en: The root *ǵneh₃- is generally reconstructed as 'to know'; it also lies behind English know, knowledge and can.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语词根 *ǵneh₃- 表示「知道」；英语的 know、knowledge 与 can 也出自这里。

items.en: Cnāwan meant 'to know, understand', and it is the direct ancestor of the modern verb know.
items.cn: cnāwan 意为「知道、懂得」，是现代动词 know 的直接祖先。

items.en: On- plus cnāwan formed oncnāwan, 'to recognize, perceive, admit'; the prefix added the idea of turning towards something.
items.cn: on- 加 cnāwan 构成 oncnāwan，意为「认出、察觉、承认」；前缀添上「转向某物」的意味。

items.en: The verb became aknowen, 'to admit, confess, recognize', as the prefix weakened to a single a-.
items.cn: 这个动词变成 aknowen，意为「承认、招认、认出」，前缀弱化成一个 a-。

items.en: The modern spelling acknowledge, with its ending modelled on knowledge, appears in the sixteenth century, often dated to the 1550s; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 现代拼写 acknowledge 的词尾仿照 knowledge 而来，十六世纪出现，通常定在十六世纪五十年代；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the old Germanic root for knowing; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of admitting and confirming.
note.cn: 形近组共享日耳曼语中表示「知道」的老词根；近义组列出其他表示承认与确认的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for what a person knows; its ending reshaped acknowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「知识、了解」，它的词尾重塑了 acknowledge 的拼写。

entries.definition: The basic verb meaning to have knowledge of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「知道、认识」，是最基本的同根词。

entries.definition: Not known or not identified; the old root with a negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未知的、不为人知的」，是老词根加否定前缀。

entries.definition: The noun for an act of admitting, thanking or confirming receipt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承认、致谢、收到确认」，是本词加名词后缀而来。

entries.definition: To agree that something is true, often unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认」，常带不情愿的意味。

entries.definition: To admit a fault or a secret, often formally or with emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坦白、招认」，多用于正式或有情绪的场合。

entries.definition: To accept that something exists or is valid; closer to the core of acknowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「认出、承认……有效」，与 acknowledge 的核心义最接近。

entries.definition: To state that something is true or has happened, especially to remove doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「确认、证实」，尤指消除疑虑。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root and the phrases the verb appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子使用真实的古英语词根，以及这个动词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: The middle of the word is knowledge: to acknowledge is to say that you know.
normal.cn: 词中间藏着 knowledge：acknowledge 就是说出「我知道」。

normal.en: Take away ac- and you have know, the oldest part of the word.
normal.cn: 去掉开头的 ac-，剩下就是 know，这是整个词最古老的部分。

normal.en: Acknowledge receipt is the phrase that runs through offices every day.
normal.cn: acknowledge receipt 是办公室里每天都会出现的说法。

normal.en: Acknowledged as means the crowd has already agreed.
normal.cn: acknowledged as 意味着众人已经一致同意。

normal.en: The spelling keeps the -ledge of knowledge, so the eye reads a word about knowing.
normal.cn: 拼写保留了 knowledge 的 -ledge，眼睛一看就知道这是关于「知道」的词。

abstract.en: Picture a nod across a room: the smallest possible way of saying I know you are here.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着房间点一下头：这是说「我知道你在」的最小方式。

abstract.en: Every sense is one person giving another person a receipt for something: a fact, a fault, a letter, a kindness.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是一个人给另一个人开一张收据：为事实、为过错、为信件、为恩情。

abstract.en: To refuse to acknowledge someone is to remove them from the world you admit to seeing.
abstract.cn: 拒绝理睬一个人，就是把他从你承认看见的世界里划掉。

examples.en: Please acknowledge my email so I know you received it.
examples.cn: 请回复确认你已收到我的邮件，好让我知道。

examples.en: He acknowledged that he had forgotten the appointment.
examples.cn: 他承认自己忘了这个约定。

examples.en: The prize was a way of acknowledging years of quiet work.
examples.cn: 这个奖是对多年默默工作的一种致意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额克闹里吉」——额头上一点，闹哄哄的场面里点个头，就是承认、确认收到。

root: 古英语 oncnāwan「认出、承认」由 on- 加 cnāwan「知道」构成，cnāwan 也是 know 与 knowledge 的来源；中古英语作 aknowen，后来词尾仿 knowledge 改成 -ledge。整个词属日耳曼语来源，没有拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of acknowledge all perform one act: making known that something has registered. What registers may be a fact, a fault, a letter, a kindness, a right, a person in the room, or a shared judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: acknowledge 的八个义项都在做同一件事：让对方知道「这件事我已登记」。被登记的可能是一个事实、一个过错、一封信、一份恩情、一项权利、房间里的一个人，或一个共同的评判。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nod that says I have seen and registered this.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个点头，表示我看见了，也记下了。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: what is already known is spoken aloud, first as fact and then as fault.
branches.cn: 真相线：心里已知的事被说出口，先是事实，后是过错。

branches.en: THE MESSAGE: recognition shrinks to a receipt when a letter or payment arrives.
branches.cn: 消息线：当信件或款项抵达，「认出」缩成一张收据。

branches.en: THE DEBT: to recognize help is to admit that something is owed.
branches.cn: 恩情线：承认帮助，也就是承认自己欠着一份情。

branches.en: THE STANDING: a right, a rank or a reputation is accepted by enough people to become real.
branches.cn: 地位线：一项权利、一个身份或一份名声，被足够多的人接受才成为现实。

branches.en: THE BODY: a nod, or the refusal to nod, shows how much recognition a person is given.
branches.cn: 身体线：点一下头，或拒绝点头，显示出一个人被给予了多少承认。

intro.en: Acknowledge is built from Old English pieces, and English suffixes extend the family.
intro.cn: acknowledge 由古英语的成分搭成，英语后缀再把这个词族扩展开。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin ancestor, so there are no Latin cognates to list here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，因此这里没有可列出的拉丁同源词。

items.example: It gave oncnāwan the sense of turning towards something.
items.exampleCN: 它让 oncnāwan 带上「转向某物」的意味。

items.example: Cnāwan is the oldest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: cnāwan 是这个词最古老的一层。

items.example: The modern verb descends from cnāwan.
items.exampleCN: 现代动词由 cnāwan 传下来。

items.example: Its ending reshaped the spelling of acknowledge.
items.exampleCN: 它的词尾重塑了 acknowledge 的拼写。

items.example: Its origin is not fully certain, but it survives in knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 它的来源不完全确定，但保存在 knowledge 里。

items.example: It is the worn-down form of on- in aknowen.
items.exampleCN: 它是 aknowen 中 on- 磨损后的形式。

definition_zh: 投资；投资额；投入；投资物
definition_en: money put into something in order to gain a profit or benefit, or the act of putting it there
core_image: 一叠钱被放进一个还在长的树坑里，等着以后长出来
scene: 老人把攒下的钱投进一家小工厂，又花两年时间教工人手艺。 The new road was a huge public investment.
sceneCN: 这里 investment 是「投资」（第 1 个义项：为获利而投入的钱或投入行为），句意为新道路是一项巨大的公共投资。画面里的物件：存折、树坑、工厂图纸。

pos.zh: 名词：投资；投资额；投入；投资物

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「投资」
由 invest 加 -or 构成，义为「投资者」
由 invest 加 -ing 构成，义为「投资行为」
同源词，义为「授职仪式」

senses.title: Money put in for gain
senses.definition: money placed in a business, property, or scheme in the hope of earning more
senses.definitionCN: 为求得更多回报而投入企业、房产或项目的钱
senses.example: She made a small investment in a friend's bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家朋友的烘焙店做了小额投资。
senses.why: Latin investire meant to clothe; the money is dressed in a new form, hoping to grow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investire 意为「给……穿衣」，钱换了件衣裳，指望长大。

senses.title: The act of putting in
senses.definition: the act or process of putting money or effort into something
senses.definitionCN: 把钱或精力投入某事的行为或过程
senses.example: Investment in new machines rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年对新机器的投资大幅上升。
senses.why: The noun can name the deed rather than the sum.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以指动作，而不指金额。

senses.title: Time or effort given
senses.definition: time, energy, or care given to something in the belief that it will pay off
senses.definitionCN: 相信会有回报而在某事上给出的时间、精力或关心
senses.example: Learning the language was an investment of three years.
senses.exampleCN: 学这门语言是三年的投入。
senses.why: Despite the money picture, the word readily counts hours as well as cash.
senses.whyCN: 尽管有金钱的画面，这个词同样能算小时，不限于现金。

senses.title: A thing invested in
senses.definition: a business, property, or asset in which money has been placed
senses.definitionCN: 已经投入资金的生意、房产或资产
senses.example: Their investments are mostly in land near the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的投资大多在城市近郊的土地上。
senses.why: By transfer the noun moves from the act to the holdings themselves.
senses.whyCN: 经转喻，名词从行为转到所持有的资产上。

intro.en: Investment comes from Latin investire, to clothe, through the idea of money put into a new dress.
intro.cn: investment 来自拉丁语 investire「给……穿衣」，经由「把钱换上新衣」的想法而来。

items.en: Vestire meant to clothe; in- meant into.
items.cn: vestire 意为穿衣，in- 意为进入。

items.en: Investire meant to dress someone in a robe of office.
items.cn: investire 意为给某人穿上就职礼袍。

items.en: English used invest for giving power or a rank.
items.cn: 英语用 invest 指授予权力或职位。

items.en: Commerce added the sense of dressing money in a venture.
items.cn: 商业又添上「把钱打扮成一项生意」义。

items.en: Investment then named the sum, the act, and the assets.
items.cn: investment 由此兼指金额、行为与资产。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invest- stem; the near-meaning group holds money words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invest- 词干；近义组收金融相关的词。

entries.definition: The verb of putting money in.
The person who puts money in.
To examine in order to find the truth.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「调查」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: Money provided for a project.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「资金」，多指拨款。

entries.definition: Money used to start or grow a business.
Money placed in a bank account.

normalIntro.en: These hooks hold on to the image of money dressed up to grow.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子抓住「钱换上衣裳去长大」的画面。

normal.en: Invest originally meant to clothe; investment dresses money in a venture.
normal.cn: invest 本义是穿衣；investment 给钱换上生意的衣裳。

normal.en: Return on investment asks whether the new clothes paid off.
normal.cn: return on investment 问的就是这身新衣有没有回本。

normal.en: You can invest money, time, or patience.
normal.cn: 钱、时间、耐心都可以 invest。

normal.en: Foreign investment moves across borders looking for growth.
normal.cn: foreign investment 越过边界寻找增长。

normal.en: Keep it apart from investigate, which follows footprints.
normal.cn: 别和 investigate 混：那个词是顺着脚印查。

abstract.en: Investment is a promise made in the form of money.
abstract.cn: 投资是用钱的形式做出的一句承诺。

abstract.en: Every tree you water is an investment in shade.
abstract.cn: 你浇的每一棵树，都是对荫凉做的投资。

abstract.en: Time is the only investment that cannot be recovered.
abstract.cn: 时间是唯一不可收回的投资。

examples.en: The factory needs foreign investment to expand.
examples.cn: 这家工厂需要外国投资才能扩张。

examples.en: Her years of study were an investment in herself.
examples.cn: 多年的学习是她对自己的投资。

examples.en: He sold his investments before the market fell.
examples.cn: 市场下跌前他卖掉了手上的投资。

dict_mnemonic.text: invest（投入）+ ment（名词）——投进去的那笔东西

root: 拉丁语 vestire「穿衣」→ investire「穿上官袍、授予」→ 英语 invest（投资），加 -ment 成 investment。同族有 invest、investor、investigate。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: money put in for gain, the act of putting in, effort given, and the assets held.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：为获利投入的钱、投入行为、付出的心力，以及所持有的资产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of money planted in a pit like a seed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠钱像种子一样被埋进土坑。

branches.en: THE BAKERY: a small sum placed in a friend's shop.
branches.cn: 烘焙店这条线：投进朋友店里的小笔钱。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: spending turned into a process.
branches.cn: 机器这条线：被当作过程来看的支出。

branches.en: THE LANGUAGE: three years paid into a skill.
branches.cn: 语言这条线：为一项技能付出的三年。

branches.en: THE LAND: the holdings the money now lives in.
branches.cn: 土地这条线：钱如今栖身的那些资产。

branches.en: THE LINK: both trust that today's cost becomes tomorrow's gain.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都相信今天的代价会换来明天的收获。

intro.en: Investment is invest plus the noun ending -ment, from Latin vestire "to clothe".
intro.cn: investment 是 invest 加名词词尾 -ment，源自拉丁语 vestire「穿衣」。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestire and investire are recorded; the money sense is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestire 与 investire 有记载，而「投资」义是英语后来添的。

definition_zh: 统治；治理；支配
definition_en: to rule a country or group, to control an organization, or to determine how something works
core_image: 船长站在船尾握着舵轮，目光越过海面看向远处的港口
scene: 这个国家由议会统治。 The country is governed by a parliament.
sceneCN: 这里 govern 是「统治、治理」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个国家由议会统治。

derivatives.zh: 政府；治理
州长；总督
治理；管理方式

senses.title: To rule
senses.definition: to control and direct the affairs of a country
senses.definitionCN: 控制并指导国家事务
senses.example: The country is governed by a parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家由议会统治。
senses.why: This is the central political sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词核心的政治含义。

senses.title: To manage
senses.definition: to direct the work of an organization or group
senses.definitionCN: 指导组织或团体的工作
senses.example: She governs the day-to-day work of the office.
senses.exampleCN: 她掌管办公室的日常工作。
senses.why: Running any body of people borrows the language of rule.
senses.whyCN: 管理任何一群人，都借用了统治的语言。

senses.title: To determine
senses.definition: to control or decide how something happens
senses.definitionCN: 控制或决定某事如何发生
senses.example: Strict rules govern how the money is spent.
senses.exampleCN: 严格的规定支配着这笔钱的使用。
senses.why: Rules steer actions just as a government steers a country.
senses.whyCN: 规则引导行动，正如政府引导国家。

intro.en: Govern began as a Latin word for steering a ship.
intro.cn: govern 最初是拉丁语中表示掌舵行船的词。

items.en: Gubernare meant to steer or pilot a ship.
items.cn: gubernare 意为掌舵、驾驶船只。

items.en: Governer kept the image of steering.
items.cn: governer 保留了掌舵的意象。

items.en: Govern entered English meaning to rule or direct.
items.cn: govern 以统治、指导之义进入英语。

items.en: It spread from states to offices and families.
items.cn: 它从国家扩展到办公室和家庭。

items.en: Rules and laws came to govern behaviour.
items.cn: 规则和法律开始支配行为。

note.en: Govern is compared with look-alike words and verbs of control.
note.cn: 把 govern 与形近词以及表示控制的动词作比较。

normalIntro.cn: govern 就是握住比自身更大的事物的舵轮。

normal.en: Fear should not govern your choices.
normal.cn: 恐惧不应支配你的选择。

abstract.cn: 善治，是掌舵而不死死抓紧。

abstract.en: Every system is governed by what it refuses to see.
abstract.cn: 每个体系都被它拒绝看见的东西所支配。

abstract.en: Power governs others; wisdom governs power.
abstract.cn: 权力统治他人，智慧统治权力。

examples.cn: 严格的规定支配着这笔钱的使用。

dict_mnemonic.text: govern 源自拉丁语 gubernare（掌舵），由「掌舵」引申为「统治、管理、支配」；government 是「政府」，governor 是「州长、总督」，governance 是「治理」，self-governing 是「自治的」。

root: 来自拉丁语 gubernare（掌舵、驾驶船只），经古法语 governer 进入英语，由掌舵的意象引申为治理国家、管理组织与支配事物。

sensesIntro.en: Govern means to rule a country, manage an organization, or determine how something works.
sensesIntro.cn: govern 指统治国家、管理组织，或支配事物如何运作。

core.en: Holding the wheel of a larger thing.
core.cn: 握住更大事物的舵轮。

branches.en: A parliament decides the fate of a nation.
branches.cn: 议会决定一个国家的命运。

branches.en: An office runs on one steady hand.
branches.cn: 一间办公室靠一只稳健的手运转。

branches.en: Written rules steer where money goes.
branches.cn: 成文规则引导资金的流向。

branches.en: A state and an office are both steered by someone.
branches.cn: 国家与办公室都由某人掌舵。

branches.en: Management and rules both decide how things happen.
branches.cn: 管理与规则都决定事情如何进行。

intro.en: Govern forms the whole family of ruling words.
intro.cn: govern 构成整个表示治理的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is gubernare, to steer, and gubernator, a steersman.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 gubernare（掌舵）和 gubernator（掌舵者）。

items.example: The country is governed by a parliament.

items.exampleCN: 一个政党治理这个地区。

items.example: The city is governed by a council.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市由市议会管理。

items.example: The government announced a new tax policy.
items.exampleCN: 政府宣布了新的税收政策。

items.example: The governor visited the new road.
items.exampleCN: 州长视察了新修的道路。

definition_zh: 批准；同意；赞许；认可；（商品）看货后再决定
definition_en: official permission for something, a favourable opinion, or an arrangement in which goods may be returned if unsatisfactory
core_image: 一枚印章落在纸面，事情从此被允许
scene: 办公桌上摊着一份方案，签字笔停在纸边。 The plan cannot start until it receives official approval.
sceneCN: 这里 approval 是「批准；同意」（第 1 个义项：官方对某事的许可）；句意为「方案必须得到正式批准才能启动」。画面里有办公桌、摊开的方案与停在纸边的签字笔。

pos.zh: 名词：批准；同意；赞许；认可

collocations.zh: 看货后再决定（不合可退）

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -al 得到的动词，义为「批准；赞成」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「赞许的」
由 approving 加 -ly 构成，义为「赞许地」
由 dis- 加 approve 构成，义为「不赞成」

senses.title: Official permission
senses.definition: official permission or agreement for a plan, request, or action
senses.definitionCN: 官方对计划、请求或行动给予的许可或同意
senses.example: The plan cannot start until it receives official approval.
senses.exampleCN: 方案必须得到正式批准才能启动。
senses.why: Approve comes from Latin approbare, 'to mark as good'; approval is the state of having been marked good.
senses.whyCN: approve 来自拉丁语 approbare「打上好之印记」；approval 就是被盖上认可之印的状态。

senses.title: A favourable opinion
senses.definition: a favourable opinion of someone or something, often shown rather than spoken
senses.definitionCN: 对某人某物的赞同看法，常以神态而非言语表现
senses.example: She smiled at him with quiet approval.
senses.exampleCN: 她朝他微笑，带着无声的赞许。
senses.why: The same stamp can be given by a look rather than by a pen.
senses.whyCN: 同一枚印章，也可以由一个眼神而不是笔来盖下。

senses.title: Goods taken on trial
senses.definition: in the phrase on approval, an arrangement in which goods are supplied and may be returned if not satisfactory
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 on approval，指先取货、不满意可退的安排
senses.example: He took the coat home on approval.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那件外套拿回家，看过再决定买不买。
senses.why: The buyer is given time to judge the goods, and only then is the stamp given.
senses.whyCN: 买方先被给了判断货物的时间，到那时才盖上那枚印章。

senses.title: The level of public support
senses.definition: the level of public support shown in polls, as in an approval rating
senses.definitionCN: 民意调查中显示的公众支持程度，如支持率
senses.example: The mayor's approval rating fell after the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工之后，市长的支持率下降了。
senses.why: Opinion polls turn scattered nods into a number, measuring how much stamping the public is willing to do.
senses.whyCN: 民意调查把零散的点头变成一个数字，衡量公众愿意盖多少认可之印。

intro.en: Approval is approve plus the noun suffix -al, and the Latin idea is a mark that says good.
intro.cn: approval 是 approve 加名词后缀 -al，拉丁观念里那是一个写着「好」的记号。

items.en: Probus means 'good, upright', and it stands behind the verb of testing and approving.
items.cn: probus 意为「好的、正直的」，它是检验与认可那个动词背后的形容词。

items.en: Probare 'to test, prove' first meant to make or show something good.
items.cn: probare「检验、证明」最初意为使某物变好，或显示出它是好的。

items.en: Ad- plus probare gave approbare, 'to assent to, to approve'.
items.cn: ad- 与 probare 构成 approbare，意为「同意、认可」。

items.en: French aprover carries the verb into English, where approve is recorded in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 aprover 把这个动词带进英语，approve 在十四世纪有记录。

items.en: The noun suffix -al turns the verb into the state or act of being approved.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -al 把动词转成被批准的状态或行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the approve family; the near-meaning group gathers words for consent and support.
note.cn: 形近组收 approve 的词族；近义组收表示同意与支持的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to permit or think well of.
entries.definitionCN: 本词由它加 -al 构成，义为「批准、赞成」的动词。

entries.definition: Showing that one thinks something is good.
Formal approval or official praise.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正式认可、嘉许」，语体更正式。

entries.definition: To think something is bad or wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不赞成」，与 approve 相对。

entries.definition: Permission given by someone with the right to refuse.
entries.definitionCN: 有拒绝权的一方给出的许可，对应 approval 的批准义。

entries.definition: The act of allowing someone to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某人做某事，比 approval 更日常。

entries.definition: Public support for a person, plan, or product.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人、某计划或产品的公开支持，对应赞许义。

entries.definition: Words expressing warm approval.
entries.definitionCN: 表达热烈赞许的话，情感比 approval 更外露。

normalIntro.en: These hooks all picture a stamp, a nod, or a poll as the same mark of good.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子都把印章、点头或民调看成同一枚「好」的记号。

normal.en: Approve plus -al: the state of being marked good.
normal.cn: approve 加 -al：被盖上好之印记的状态。

normal.en: An official stamp says the plan may begin.
normal.cn: 一枚公章的印记说：方案可以开始了。

normal.en: A quiet smile can give approval without words.
normal.cn: 一个安静的微笑，可以不用说话就表示赞许。

normal.en: Goods on approval are worn before the stamp.
normal.cn: 看货再决定的商品，是先穿戴、后盖印。

normal.en: An approval rating turns nods into numbers.
normal.cn: 支持率把点头变成数字。

abstract.en: Permission, praise and popularity are all versions of one mark.
abstract.cn: 许可、赞许与人气，都是同一枚印记的变体。

abstract.en: The word shows how a judgement becomes a document.
abstract.cn: 这个词展示了判断如何变成一纸文书。

abstract.en: To approve is always to say that something is good enough.
abstract.cn: 批准，始终是在说某物足够好。

examples.en: The plan cannot start until it receives official approval.
examples.cn: 方案必须得到正式批准才能启动。

examples.en: She smiled at him with quiet approval.
examples.cn: 她朝他微笑，带着无声的赞许。

examples.en: He took the coat home on approval.
examples.cn: 他把那件外套拿回家，看过再决定买不买。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普罗沃」——红章一盖，纸上写着可以：批准；赞许

root: approval 由 approve 加名词后缀 -al 构成。approve 来自拉丁语 approbare「同意、认可」，其形容词 probus 意为「好的、正直的」，动词 probare 则是检验并显示其好。因此 approval 的核心意象始终是「给某物盖上好之印记」：官方盖印就是批准，一个眼神盖印就是赞许，商品先拿回家再盖印就是看货后决定，而民意调查则把这枚印记换算成支持率。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all give the mark of good: an official stamp, a friendly look, goods kept on trial, and a poll number.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都在盖上「好」的印记：官方批文、友善的目光、试用后再买的商品，以及民调数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red seal pressed onto paper, turning a proposal into a permission.
core.cn: 核心意象：红章压到纸上，把一份提案变成一项许可。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT LINE: the official stamp allows the plan to start.
branches.cn: 文书线：官方印章让方案得以启动。

branches.en: THE LOOK LINE: a smile gives the stamp without a pen.
branches.cn: 目光线：一个微笑不用笔就盖了印。

branches.en: THE TRIAL LINE: the buyer judges before the stamp is given.
branches.cn: 试用线：买方先判断，之后才盖印。

branches.en: THE POLL LINE: scattered nods are counted as a number.
branches.cn: 民调线：零散的点头被计成一个数字。

branches.en: THE TRUST LINE: official and personal approval both build confidence.
branches.cn: 信任线：官方与私人的认可都在建立信心。

intro.en: Approval is a regular verb-plus-suffix noun, and its parts are still transparent.
intro.cn: approval 是规则的动词加后缀名词，各部分仍然透明。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is genuine: probus 'good' and probare 'to test' sit inside approbare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：probus「好的」与 probare「检验」就在 approbare 里面。

items.meaning: to permit or think well of
items.example: The board will approve the request.
items.exampleCN: 董事会将批准这项请求。

items.example: She gave him an approving glance.
items.exampleCN: 她向他投去赞许的一瞥。

items.example: He nodded approvingly at the draft.
items.exampleCN: 他对着草稿赞许地点头。

items.exampleCN: 她的姑母不赞成这个计划。

items.example: His parents approve of the marriage.
items.exampleCN: 他的父母认可这桩婚事。

items.example: The design earned the director's seal of approval.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计获得了主管的认可。

items.meaning: with the right to return goods
items.meaningCN: 看货后再决定（不合可退）
items.example: The books were sent on approval.
items.exampleCN: 这些书是看货后再决定是否购买的。

definition_zh: 乙醇；酒精；醇类；酒类；含酒精饮料；消毒酒精
definition_en: the chemical ethanol, the class of organic compounds it belongs to, drinks that contain it, or the liquid used for cleaning and as a fuel
core_image: 一只透明细颈瓶，清亮的液体几乎看不见，只在瓶壁上留下一道亮痕
scene: 厨房台面上放着一小瓶透明液体，旁边的棉球和纱布还没收好，窗外的光穿过瓶子，在桌面上留下一道亮痕。 She cleaned the cut with a little alcohol before putting on a plaster.
sceneCN: 这里 alcohol 是「消毒酒精」（第 4 个义项：外用的乙醇制剂）；句意为她先用一点酒精清洁伤口，再贴上创可贴。画面里是透明瓶、棉球、纱布与桌上的亮痕。

pos.zh: 名词：乙醇；酒精；醇类；酒类；消毒酒精

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -ic 构成，义为「含酒精的」；作名词指「酗酒者、酒精依赖者」
由 alcoholic 去掉 -ic 加后缀 -ism 构成，义为「酒精依赖、酗酒」
由本词加后缀 -free 构成，义为「不含酒精的」，多用于饮料标签
由本词加后缀 -ate 构成，义为「醇化物」，是化学中指醇与金属或碱结合的产物的术语

senses.title: The chemical ethanol
senses.titleCN: 乙醇：酒精这种化学物质
senses.definition: a clear flammable liquid, the intoxicating substance in drinks and a common solvent and fuel
senses.definitionCN: 一种无色易燃的液体，是酒类中的致醉成分，也常用作溶剂与燃料
senses.example: The lab stores pure alcohol in a locked cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把纯酒精锁在柜子里。
senses.why: Modern chemistry fixed the old word onto one molecule, so alcohol now names ethanol itself, whether it comes from a still or a factory.
senses.whyCN: 现代化学把这个古老的词固定在一个分子上，于是 alcohol 现在指乙醇本身，无论它来自蒸馏器还是工厂。

senses.title: The class of alcohols
senses.titleCN: 醇类：含羟基的有机化合物
senses.definition: any member of a large class of organic compounds containing a hydroxyl group, such as methanol or ethanol
senses.definitionCN: 含羟基的一大类有机化合物中的任何一种，如甲醇或乙醇
senses.example: The course compares alcohols with acids and ethers.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课把醇类与酸、醚作比较。
senses.why: Once chemists saw that many liquids share the same reactive group, the name had to stretch from one substance to a whole family.
senses.whyCN: 当化学家发现许多液体共有同一个反应基团时，这个名字就必须从一种物质扩展到整个家族。

senses.title: Drinks that contain it
senses.definition: alcoholic drinks taken together, such as beer, wine and spirits
senses.definitionCN: 合起来看的含酒精饮料，如啤酒、葡萄酒与烈酒
senses.example: The hotel does not serve alcohol after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆午夜之后不再供应酒。
senses.why: People met the substance mainly in what they drank, so the name of the liquid became the name of the drinks that carry it.
senses.whyCN: 人们主要通过饮品接触这种物质，于是液体的名字变成了承载它的那些饮品的名字。

senses.title: The liquid used for cleaning
senses.titleCN: 消毒酒精：外用的乙醇制剂
senses.definition: a solution of ethanol used outside the body to clean skin, tools or surfaces, or as a solvent
senses.definitionCN: 用于体表、器具或表面清洁的乙醇溶液，也可作溶剂
senses.example: Wipe the thermometer with alcohol before you use it.
senses.exampleCN: 使用温度计之前先用酒精擦一擦。
senses.why: The same molecule that makes a drink intoxicating kills germs, so a household bottle of alcohol belongs to the cleaning shelf rather than the bar.
senses.whyCN: 让饮品致醉的同一个分子也能杀菌，所以家里那瓶酒精放在清洁架上，而不是酒柜里。

senses.title: Strong distilled spirits
senses.titleCN: 烈酒：蒸馏而成的高度酒
senses.definition: strong drink produced by distillation, such as whisky, brandy or vodka, rather than beer or wine
senses.definitionCN: 经蒸馏制成的高度酒，如威士忌、白兰地或伏特加，与啤酒、葡萄酒相对
senses.example: Vodka is a strong alcohol distilled from grain or potatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 伏特加是用谷物或马铃薯蒸馏而成的高度酒。
senses.why: Distillation concentrates the spirit, and English often uses alcohol for the strong result, the drink where the substance is most obvious.
senses.whyCN: 蒸馏把酒精度提了上去，英语常用 alcohol 指蒸馏出来的高度酒，也就是那种物质最显眼的饮品。

intro.en: Alcohol travelled from an Arabic word for a dark eye powder to the name of a clear liquid, through medieval Latin and early chemistry.
intro.cn: alcohol 从一个指深色眼妆粉的阿拉伯词，经中世纪拉丁语与早期化学，走到了指一种清澈液体的名称。

items.en: Kuhl was powdered antimony, a dark mineral used as eye cosmetic; the word named the powder, not a drink.
items.cn: kuhl 指锑的粉末，是一种用作眼妆的深色矿物；这个词指粉末，不是饮品。

items.en: With the definite article al-, al-kuhl meant 'the kuhl'; the article is the al- at the front of the modern word.
items.cn: 加上定冠词 al- 后，al-kuhl 意为「那种锑粉」；这个冠词就是现代词开头的 al-。

items.en: Medieval Latin borrowed alcohol for antimony powder and then widened it to any fine powder or distilled essence.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语借入 alcohol 指锑粉，随后扩展到任何细粉或蒸馏所得的精华。

items.en: English alcohol first meant a fine powder made by sublimation; the phrase alcohol of wine for distilled spirit is recorded in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语 alcohol 最初指升华制成的细粉；十七世纪有 alcohol of wine 的说法，指蒸馏所得的酒之精华。

items.en: Around 1800 chemistry fixed alcohol on ethanol and on the class of alcohols; the older sense of strong drink survives in everyday use.
items.cn: 约在十九世纪初，化学把 alcohol 固定在乙醇与醇类上；较早的「烈酒」义仍在日常用法中留存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers English words built from alcohol; the near-meaning group gathers the chemical name, the drinks and the informal words for them.
note.cn: 形近组收由 alcohol 构成的英语词；近义组收化学名称、酒类以及它们口语化的说法。

entries.definition: Containing alcohol, or a person dependent on it; formed with the suffix -ic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「含酒精的」；作名词指「酒精依赖者」，由本词加后缀 -ic 构成。

entries.definition: The condition of being unable to control drinking; formed with the suffix -ism.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酒精依赖、酗酒」，指无法控制饮酒的状况，由本词加后缀 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: A drink with no alcohol in it; the negative prefix non- is added to alcoholic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不含酒精的」，指饮品中没有酒精；是加否定前缀 non- 构成。

entries.definition: A label meaning that a product contains no alcohol at all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无酒精的」，是产品标签上的说法，表示完全不含酒精。

entries.definition: An instrument for measuring how much alcohol a liquid contains; built from alcohol plus meter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酒精比重计」，指测量液体酒精含量的仪器，由 alcohol 加 meter 构成。

entries.definition: The systematic chemical name for the alcohol in drinks and in fuel blends.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「乙醇」，是酒类与燃料混合液中所含酒精的化学系统名称。

entries.definition: Strong alcoholic drink, especially distilled spirits; more formal than booze.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烈酒、酒」，尤指蒸馏酒，比口语词更正式。

entries.definition: Distilled drinks such as whisky or gin; the word keeps the old image of a distilled essence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烈酒」，如威士忌或杜松子酒；这个词仍保留着「蒸馏出的精华」这一古老意象。

entries.definition: An informal word for alcohol or a drinking session.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酒、喝酒」，是口语说法。

entries.definition: Any liquid you swallow; in social use it can mean an alcoholic one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「饮料」，泛指任何可饮用的液体；在社交语境里也可专指含酒精的饮品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Arabic source, the article hidden at the front, and the chemistry that reshaped the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的阿拉伯语来源、藏在词首的冠词，以及重塑了词义的化学。

normal.en: Al-kuhl was antimony powder for the eyes: the word began as a mineral powder, not as a drink.
normal.cn: al-kuhl 是画眼用的锑粉：这个词起初是矿物粉末，不是饮品。

normal.en: The al- at the front is simply the Arabic word for 'the', so alcohol literally contains a definite article.
normal.cn: 开头的 al- 就是阿拉伯语的定冠词「那个」，所以 alcohol 字面上含着一个定冠词。

normal.en: Chemistry split the word in two: alcohol is ethanol, while alcohols are the whole class.
normal.cn: 化学把这个词分成两层：alcohol 指乙醇，alcohols 指整个醇类。

normal.en: Distillation is the hinge: it concentrates the spirit and gives the word its strong-drink sense.
normal.cn: 蒸馏是转轴：它把酒之精华浓缩起来，也让这个词有了「烈酒」义。

normal.en: Rubbing alcohol goes on cotton wool, not into a glass; the same word changes shelf.
normal.cn: rubbing alcohol 是倒在棉球上的，不是倒进杯里的；同一个词换了一个货架。

abstract.en: Picture a dark powder being sieved in an old pharmacy, then a clear liquid in a glass vial on a lab bench.
abstract.cn: 想象老药房里有人在筛深色粉末，再想象实验台上一只装着清亮液体的玻璃小瓶。

abstract.en: One word covers a molecule, a chemical class, a drink and a cleaner: the same substance seen from four distances.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖一个分子、一个化学类别、一种饮品和一瓶清洁剂：同一种物质在四个距离上被看见。

abstract.en: The long road from eye powder to fuel shows how a name can travel until only the substance remains.
abstract.cn: 从眼妆粉到燃料的漫长道路说明：一个名字可以一路迁徙，最后只剩下它所指的是那种物质。

examples.en: This drink contains no alcohol at all.
examples.cn: 这种饮料完全不含酒精。

examples.en: Rubbing alcohol is kept in the first-aid box.
examples.cn: 外用消毒酒精放在急救箱里。

examples.en: Yeast turns sugar into alcohol during fermentation.
examples.cn: 发酵过程中，酵母把糖变成酒精。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿尔科霍尔」——阿尔是冠词，科霍尔是锑粉：从画眼的粉末走到清亮的酒。

root: alcohol 来自阿拉伯语 al-kuhl，其中 al- 是定冠词，kuhl 指用作眼妆的锑粉。中世纪拉丁语借作 alcohol，先指锑粉，再泛指细粉与蒸馏所得的精华；英语十六世纪借入，十七世纪用它指蒸馏酒，十九世纪化学把它固定为乙醇及醇类。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move outward from one substance: ethanol itself, the whole chemical class, the drinks that carry it, the bottle used for cleaning, and the strong spirits produced by distillation.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从一种物质向外展开：乙醇本身、整个化学类别、承载它的酒类、用于清洁的那瓶液体，以及蒸馏出的烈酒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine powder is distilled into a clear liquid that can clean, burn or intoxicate.
core.cn: 核心意象：细粉被蒸馏成一种清亮液体，它能清洁、能燃烧，也能使人醉。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE: chemistry fixes the old word on ethanol, a clear flammable liquid.
branches.cn: 分子线：化学把这个古老的词固定在乙醇上，一种无色易燃的液体。

branches.en: THE CLASS: the name stretches from one substance to every compound with the same group.
branches.cn: 类别线：名字从一种物质扩展到所有含同一基团的化合物。

branches.en: THE DRINK: the substance is met mainly in beer, wine and spirits, so the word names them.
branches.cn: 饮品线：人们主要在啤酒、葡萄酒与烈酒中接触这种物质，于是这个词也指这些饮品。

branches.en: THE CLEANER: the same liquid kills germs, so a bottle of it sits with cotton wool and bandages.
branches.cn: 清洁线：同一种液体能杀菌，于是那瓶东西与棉球、绷带放在一起。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: distillation concentrates the drink and produces the strong spirits the word often means.
branches.cn: 烈酒线：蒸馏浓缩了饮品，造出这个词常指的烈性酒。

intro.en: Alcohol is a borrowing whose Arabic article is still visible; English and chemistry then add suffixes and prefixes to build the modern family.
intro.cn: alcohol 是一个借词，阿拉伯语冠词至今可见；英语与化学再用后缀、前缀构造现代词族。

latinIntro.en: The medieval Latin noun alcohol is recorded with the powder and distillate senses; the Arabic source is given beside it because the word is not native Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语名词 alcohol 有粉末与蒸馏物两种义项的记录；由于它不是拉丁语本族词，阿拉伯语来源一并列出。

senses.title: A place for drinks
senses.definition: a place where people buy and drink alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 人们购买并饮用酒类的场所
senses.example: They met at a small bar near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站附近的一家小酒吧见面。
senses.why: A bar is first a counter, and the room around that counter became the drinking place.
senses.whyCN: bar 首先指柜台，围着柜台的空间就成了喝酒的地方。

senses.title: A long piece
senses.definition: a long straight piece of metal, wood or other material
senses.definitionCN: 一段细长的金属、木头或其他材料
senses.example: He broke off a bar of chocolate.
senses.exampleCN: 他掰下了一块巧克力。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a straight beam or rod, from Old French barre, and long shapes still carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是笔直的横木或杆，来自古法语 barre，细长的东西至今沿用这个词。

senses.title: To block
senses.definition: to block movement or prevent something from happening
senses.definitionCN: 阻挡通行或阻止某事发生
senses.example: A fallen tree barred the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵倒下的树挡住了路。
senses.why: A bar across a door stops people, so the noun turned into a verb meaning to block.
senses.whyCN: 横在门上的木条能挡住人，于是名词转为动词，表示阻挡。

definition_zh: 代表；表现；描绘；陈述；代表权
definition_en: the act of speaking or acting for others, or something such as an image or statement that stands for something else
core_image: 一张地图把整片山河缩在纸上，每个符号都对应真实的一处地方
scene: 律师翻着案卷，指出这份笔录没有准确反映当事人的原话。 The lawyer argued that the representation of her words was unfair.
sceneCN: 这里 representation 是「描绘；表述」（第 2 个义项：以图像或文字再现某事物）；句意：律师认为对当事人原话的表述并不公平。

derivatives.zh: 代表；描绘
代表
具象的；表现的

senses.title: The act of acting for others
senses.definition: the act of speaking or acting officially for a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 正式替一群人说或做的行为
senses.example: The region demands fair representation in parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区要求在议会中获得公平的代表权。
senses.why: The noun names the action behind represent, and the political sense is the oldest public use.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词给 represent 背后的动作命名，其中政治代表义是最早的公共用法。

senses.title: An image or description
senses.definition: a picture, model, or description that shows something
senses.definitionCN: 展示某事物的图画、模型或描述
senses.example: The chart is a visual representation of the data.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图表是数据的可视化表现。
senses.why: A representation makes something present to the eye, so the product of showing becomes a sense of its own.
senses.whyCN: 表现让某物在眼前呈现，于是「呈现出来的成品」本身也成为一个义项。

senses.title: A formal statement
senses.definition: a formal statement made to an authority in order to influence a decision
senses.definitionCN: 向权威机构作出的正式陈述，用以影响决定
senses.example: The group made representations to the council about the road.
senses.exampleCN: 该团体就这条路向议会提出了陈述。
senses.why: Speaking for a group can take the form of an official statement, which inherits the same word.
senses.whyCN: 替群体发言可以采取正式陈述的形式，于是沿用了同一个词。

senses.title: Legal acting for a client
senses.definition: the work of a lawyer who speaks and acts for a client in a case
senses.definitionCN: 律师在案件中替当事人发言和行事的工作
senses.example: He cannot afford legal representation.
senses.exampleCN: 他请不起法律代理。
senses.why: Legal representation is a specialised branch of acting for someone else.
senses.whyCN: 法律代理是「替他人行事」的一个专门分支。

intro.en: Representation comes from Latin repraesentatio, the noun of repraesentare, to make present.
intro.cn: representation 来自拉丁名词 repraesentatio，是 repraesentare（使在场）的名词形式。

items.en: Repraesentare means to bring something before the eyes or mind.
items.cn: repraesentare 意为把某物带到眼前或心中。

items.en: Repraesentatio names the act of showing or making present.
items.cn: repraesentatio 指展示或使在场的动作。

items.en: Old French representation keeps the senses of image and official statement.
items.cn: 古法语 representation 保留「图像」和「正式陈述」两种含义。

items.en: Middle English representation is used for pictures, symbols, and spokesmen.
items.cn: 中古英语 representation 用于图画、符号和代言人。

items.en: Political writing develops the sense of elected representation.
items.cn: 政治写作发展出「选举代表制」的含义。

items.en: Modern English adds legal representation and data representation.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了法律代理和数据表示等用法。

note.en: Representation is the noun product of represent, and it is close to words for images, symbols, and formal statements.
note.cn: representation 是 represent 的名词产物，与表示图像、符号和正式陈述的词相邻。
